rules.description: The undisputed core anchor of the design, providing maximum contrast for text and primary actions.
when_to_use: Primary CTA backgrounds (e.g., 'Sign up' and 'Play' buttons)
Main typography, including hero headings and body copy

rules.description: A comprehensive suite of surface colors ranging from pure white to warm cream, dictating the structural hierarchy of the page without using heavy lines.
when_to_use: Large feature sections and bento box card backgrounds (#F5F3F1 'Cream')
Floating agent widgets and secondary CTA buttons (#FFFFFF)

rules.description: The primary utility gray for establishing typographic hierarchy, keeping secondary information legible without competing with headings.
when_to_use: Footer category headers and inactive footer links
Timestamps and metadata on blog cards

rules.description: A soft, low-contrast gray reserved for tertiary UI hints and disabled or subtle states.
A dark charcoal gray that bridges the gap between the stark black headings and the lighter slate descriptions.
when_to_use: Dense mock-UI paragraph text inside product graphics

insights: Extreme Neutrality: The brand completely eschews saturated hues in its UI, relying entirely on a sophisticated spectrum of blacks, grays, and warm creams to evoke a highly premium, editorial, and enterprise-ready aesthetic.

Surface-Driven Hierarchy: Instead of relying on borders or lines to separate content, the design structures the page by alternating large background blocks (pure white vs. cream #F5F3F1), creating a soft, uninterrupted reading experience.

Strategic Contrast: Because the environment is entirely neutral, pitch-black CTA buttons carry immense visual weight. They don't need a bright color to stand out because they are the darkest elements on an otherwise light, airy page.
